primary_sections.text:
Write $\rho_p=\operatorname{diag}(1-p,p)$ for a diagonal qubit state. Set $a=\pi/12$ and
$$\mathcal S_a=\{\rho_{\sin^2\theta}:a\le\theta\le\pi/4\},\qquad T_a(\rho_{\sin^2\theta})=\rho_{\sin^2(\theta-a)}.$$
On this family, $T_a$ preserves root fidelity and contracts trace distance for every pair, but it sends the finite input relative entropy $D(\rho_{\sin^2(\pi/4)}\|\rho_{\sin^2 a})$ to $D(\rho_{\sin^2(\pi/4-a)}\|\rho_0)=+\infty$. The map is nonlinear and is not the restriction of a quantum channel. Thus metric inequalities on a family under an arbitrary map do not by themselves prove quantum-relative-entropy data processing for channels.

As a separate support check, $|0\rangle\langle0|$ and $|+\rangle\langle+|$ have root fidelity and trace distance both $1/\sqrt2$, while $D(|0\rangle\langle0|\| |+\rangle\langle+|)=+\infty$.

Let $T$ be a positive-definite endomorphism of a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $K$, and let $V:H\to K$ be an isometry from a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. Define $\log T$ by the natural logarithm of the positive eigenvalues in the finite spectral decomposition. Then
$$-\log(V^\dagger TV)\preceq V^\dagger(-\log T)V.$$

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space with inner product linear in its first argument, and let $A,B\in\operatorname{End}(H)$ be positive definite. Equip $\operatorname{End}(H)$ with $\langle X,Y\rangle_{HS}:=\operatorname{tr}(XY^\dagger)$, define $L_B(X)=BX$ and $R_{A^{-1}}(X)=XA^{-1}$, and put $\Delta_{B,A}=L_BR_{A^{-1}}$. Then $\Delta_{B,A}$ is positive definite and
$$\langle(-\log\Delta_{B,A})A^{1/2},A^{1/2}\rangle_{HS}=D(A\Vert B).$$
All logarithms are the natural spectral logarithms on positive eigenvalues.

Let $H_A,H_B,H_C$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a density operator on their ordered tensor product. Write $\rho_{AB},\rho_{BC},\rho_B$ for its marginals using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. Then
$$S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})\ge S(\rho_B)+S(\rho_{ABC}),$$
where $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho)$ with $0\ln0:=0$ as in [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

Let $H_A,H_B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $d=\dim H_B\ge1$, and let $A,B$ be non-negative operators on $H_A\otimes H_B$. Then

$$D(\operatorname{Tr}_B A\|\operatorname{Tr}_B B)\le D(A\|B).$$

For three qubit registers $A,B,C$, let
$$|\mathrm{GHZ}\rangle=(|000\rangle+|111\rangle)/\sqrt2,\qquad \rho_{ABC}=|\mathrm{GHZ}\rangle\langle\mathrm{GHZ}|.$$
Each one-register marginal and each two-register marginal has entropy $\ln2$, while $S(\rho_{ABC})=0$. In particular, for the displayed order,
$$S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})=2\ln2>\ln2=S(\rho_B)+S(\rho_{ABC}),$$
so strong subadditivity is strict.

For a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N:A\to B$, define

$$f_{\mathcal N}(\rho):=S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),\qquad F(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}f_{\mathcal N}(\rho).$$

For any two finite-dimensional channels $\mathcal N_i:A_i\to B_i$,

$$F(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)=F(\mathcal N_1)+F(\mathcal N_2).$$

primary_sections.text: Let $V:\mathbb C^d\to B\otimes E$ be a Stinespring isometry and $\tau=I_d/d$. Every $0<R<I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)$ is achievable by isometric subspace entanglement transmission. If the coherent information is nonpositive, the lower bound is supplied by the one-dimensional code. Here an $n$-use code has an isometry $W_n:\mathbb C^{K_n}\to A^{\otimes n}$ and a CPTP decoder to $\mathbb C^{K_n}$; its squared overlap with the maximally entangled target tends to one and $n^{-1}\ln K_n\to R$. The same conclusion holds for a flat state on any nonzero input subspace by composing with its embedding.

primary_sections.text:
Let $x\mapsto\rho_x$ be a finite-input, finite-output memoryless cq channel as in [[def-it-classical-quantum-memoryless-channel]]. With the average-error code convention of [[def-it-cq-channel-block-code-and-error]], its classical capacity in nats per use is
$$C_{\rm cq}=\max_{p\in\Delta(\mathcal X)}\chi_p,\qquad \chi_p:=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$
For every $0\le R<C_{\rm cq}$ a sequence of codes with rate tending to $R$ has average error tending to zero, and every reliable sequence has limiting upper rate at most $C_{\rm cq}$. This theorem concerns a fixed finite classical input alphabet and does not assert a single-letter formula for general quantum-input channels.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channel. For each $n\ge1$, let

$$p_n(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\mathcal E_n} I_p(\mathcal E_n,\mathcal N^{\otimes n}),$$

where the supremum ranges over all finite ensembles of input states on $A^{\otimes n}$. Under the strong-secrecy, average-error convention in [[def-it-quantum-channel-operational-capacities]],

$$P(\mathcal N)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{p_n(\mathcal N)}n=\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{p_n(\mathcal N)}n.$$

This statement is regularized and asserts no general single-letter formula.

primary_sections.text:
Let a binary cq channel send equiprobable pure qubit states $|\psi_0\rangle,|\psi_1\rangle$ with overlap magnitude $c=|\langle\psi_0,\psi_1\rangle|\in[0,1]$. This ensemble has Holevo information
$$\chi=h\!\left(\frac{1+c}{2}\right)\quad\text{nats per channel use},$$
where $h(t)=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t)$ with $0\ln0:=0$. If $\chi>0$, every rate $R$ with $0\le R<\chi$ is achievable for this memoryless channel; if $c=1$, the states coincide and no positive rate follows from this ensemble.

Let $\mathcal N_i:A_i\to B_i$ for $i=1,2$ be finite-dimensional degradable channels with complements $\mathcal N_i^c=\mathcal D_i\circ\mathcal N_i$. Then $\rho\mapsto I_c(\rho,\mathcal N_i)$ is concave and nonnegative. For every joint input state $\rho_{A_1A_2}$,

$$I_c(\rho_{A_1A_2},\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)\le I_c(\rho_{A_1},\mathcal N_1)+I_c(\rho_{A_2},\mathcal N_2).$$

Consequently the supremum coherent information of $\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2$ is the sum of the two single-channel suprema.

primary_sections.text:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel. Under the shared-entanglement coding convention in [[def-it-quantum-channel-operational-capacities]],

$$C_E(\mathcal N)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}\bigl(S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)\bigr)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}I(R;B)_{(\operatorname{id}_R\otimes\mathcal N)(\psi_\rho)},$$

where $\psi_\rho$ is any finite purification of $\rho$ on $R\otimes A$. The value is additive: $C_E(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)=C_E(\mathcal N_1)+C_E(\mathcal N_2)$ for finite-dimensional channels.

primary_sections.text:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set, let $(p_x)$ be a probability vector, let $\rho_x$ be density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional space $H_B$, and let $\bar\rho:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. For a finite POVM $(E_y)_{y\in Y}$ on $H_B$, define $w(y\mid x):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_xE_y)$, $q_y:=\sum_xp_xw(y\mid x)$, and the classical mutual information

$$I(X:Y):=\sum_{x,y:p_xw(y\mid x)>0}p_xw(y\mid x)\ln\frac{w(y\mid x)}{q_y}.$$

Then

$$I(X:Y)\le\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\})=S(\bar\rho)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channel. For $n\ge1$, put

$$q_n(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A^{\otimes n})}I_c(\rho,\mathcal N^{\otimes n}).$$

Under the subspace entanglement-transmission convention in [[def-it-quantum-channel-operational-capacities]],

$$Q(\mathcal N)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{q_n(\mathcal N)}n=\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{q_n(\mathcal N)}n.$$

No general single-letter or additivity assertion is made.

primary_sections.text: Write $h(t)=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t)$ with continuous endpoints. Let $g(t)=(1+t)\ln(1+t)-t\ln t$ for $t\in[0,1]$, with $g(0)=0$. For states $\rho,\sigma$ on dimension $d\ge1$ and $t=\frac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$, $$|S(\rho)-S(\sigma)|\le t\ln d+g(t).$$ Moreover, if $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_M$ are states on that space and $a=M^{-1}\sum_m\frac12\|\sigma_m-\sigma\|_1$, their uniform Holevo information is at most $2a\ln d+2g(a)$. In particular on dimension $d_E^n$, exponential decay of $a$ makes unnormalized Holevo information tend to zero.

primary_sections.text: Let $\rho$ be a state on dimension $d$ and $\mathcal N$ a finite-dimensional channel. There is an exact decomposition $\rho^{\otimes n}=\sum_t p_t\tau_t$ into mutually orthogonal flat spectral-type states, with at most $(n+1)^d$ positive-weight types and $H(T)\le d\ln(n+1)$. For its fixed complementary channel, $$\sum_t p_t I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})\ge nI_c(\rho,\mathcal N)-H(T),$$ $$\sum_t p_t[S(\tau_t)+I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})]\ge n[S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)]-2H(T).$$ Thus in each inequality some flat type state attains at least the displayed lower bound.

primary_sections.text: Fix any finite input ensemble $(p_x,\rho_x)$ for a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N$ and a complement $\mathcal N^c$. Let $\chi_B,\chi_E$ be the Holevo informations of their output ensembles. Every $0<R<\chi_B-\chi_E$ admits uniform $M_n$-message codes with mixed input states, Bob POVMs, $n^{-1}\ln M_n\to R$, average error tending to zero, and unnormalized complementary-output Holevo leakage tending to zero. The construction has exponentially decaying average error and average trace distance to a fixed complementary product target; dimension-dependent entropy control converts the latter to strong Holevo secrecy.
